title: Effect of a Silent Dropper Action
statement: Let $x$ be a Boolean word; let $q,q'$ be optional states among six control states; let $i,i',n$ be natural numbers; let $h,h'$ be integers; let $m,d$ be input-head and counter-head moves; let $b$ be an optional output bit; and let $o$ be an output word. Suppose moving the input head by $m$ from the clamped offset $i$ gives the clamped offset $i'$, and $h+d=h'$. Applying the action with these moves, no counter write, output bit $b$, and successor state $q'$ to the canonical configuration with state $q$, offset $i$, counter length $n$, head $h$, and output $o$ gives the canonical configuration with state $q'$, offset $i'$, counter length $n$, head $h'$, and output $o$ followed by $b$ when present.
hypotheses_covered: input-head movement takes clamped offset $i$ to clamped offset $i'$
replaced:
Let $x$ be an input, and consider a dropper action with no counter write, input
move $m$, counter-head move $d$, optional output bit $b$, and target state $q'$.
If the move $m$ takes the clamped offset $i$ to the clamped offset $i'$, and
$h + d = h'$, then applying the action to the canonical dropper configuration at
offset $i$ with counter length $n$, counter head $h$, and output $o$ yields the
canonical configuration in state $q'$ at offset $i'$ with the same counter, head
at $h'$, and output $o$ followed by $b$ when present.
